question: What is the primary characteristic of Type III Female Genital Mutilation, also known as infibulation?

options.A: Complete surgical removal of the uterus and ovaries
options.B: Narrowing of the vaginal orifice with creation of a covering seal
options.C: Scraping of the vaginal walls to induce scarring
options.D: Piercing of the clitoris without tissue removal

explanation: Type III FGM involves cutting and apposing the labia to create a seal, leaving only a tiny opening for urine and menstrual flow. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why does the World Health Organization classify procedures like ritual pricking or piercing of the genitalia under Type IV FGM?

options.A: Because they are exclusively performed in sterile hospital environments
options.B: Because they cause permanent anatomical closure of the vaginal canal
options.C: Because they represent all other harmful non-medical genital modifications not covered in types I to III
options.D: Because they involve significant removal of erectile tissue

explanation: Type IV serves as a catch-all category for miscellaneous harmful genital practices that do not fit the specific tissue excision patterns of the first three types. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which immediate complication is most directly linked to the use of unsterile cutting instruments and traditional topical applications during FGM?
explanation: Crude instruments and contaminated traditional substances introduce pathogens directly into fresh surgical wounds, leading to high rates of localized infection and systemic sepsis. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h2)

question: A young girl presents to the emergency clinic shortly after undergoing FGM with bright red blood spurting from the wound site. Which anatomical vessel is most likely injured?
explanation: The high vascularity of the clitoris makes the dorsal clitoral artery particularly vulnerable to severe laceration during tissue removal. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the term for the accumulation of menstrual blood trapped behind a scarred or narrowed vaginal opening caused by infibulation?
explanation: Hematocolpos describes the pooling of menstrual fluid inside the vagina because the scarred or sealed introitus prevents normal egress. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why do women with Type III FGM experience a high frequency of recurrent urinary tract infections?

options.A: Scar tissue distortion and mechanical obstruction near the urethral meatus impede free urine flow
options.B: The absence of the labia causes permanent bladder hypermobility
options.C: Frequent catheterization is required for basic daily hygiene
options.D: Hormonal imbalances suppress local immune responses in the urinary bladder

explanation: When scar tissue narrows or obstructs the urethral outlet, incomplete bladder emptying promotes bacterial proliferation and recurrent infections. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h3)

question: A laboring woman with a history of Type III FGM experiences prolonged second-stage labor. What is the primary mechanical reason for this delay?

options.A: Rigid, inelastic scar tissue obstructing the normal descent of the fetal head
options.B: Fetal malposition caused by maternal pelvic narrowing
options.C: Premature rupture of membranes leading to dry labor
options.D: Inadequate uterine contractions caused by oxytocin receptor exhaustion

explanation: The dense fibrotic tissue created by infibulation fails to stretch during delivery, creating a physical barrier that traps the fetus. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which surgical procedure is frequently necessary during the childbirth of an infibulated woman to facilitate safe delivery?
explanation: Defibulation involves cutting open the fused scar tissue of the vaginal opening to allow safe passage for the infant during labor. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which psychological condition is most commonly documented among survivors of childhood FGM?
explanation: The severe physical pain and psychological shock experienced during the procedure often manifest as long-term post-traumatic stress symptoms. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary physiological and anatomical reason for sexual dysfunction in women who have undergone clitoridectomy?

options.A: Loss of highly sensitive erectile nerve endings
options.B: Permanent closure of the Bartholin glands
options.C: Hypertrophy of the surrounding pelvic floor muscles
options.D: Complete atrophy of the vaginal rugae

explanation: The clitoris contains a dense concentration of nerve endings responsible for sexual arousal and sensation; its removal directly diminishes sexual response. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h5)

question: What approach is most effective when a nurse is conducting a health history on a patient who has experienced FGM?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on surgical repair options without discussing symptoms
options.B: Conducting the interview in an open ward to maintain total transparency
options.C: Using trauma-informed, non-judgmental communication to build trust
options.D: Avoiding questions about the genitalia entirely to prevent patient embarrassment

explanation: Trauma-informed care prioritizes emotional safety and trust, which encourages vulnerable patients to disclose sensitive health histories. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which clinical action is NOT appropriate during the initial nursing assessment of a patient with suspected FGM complications?

options.A: Providing a private and culturally safe environment for the examination
options.B: Inquiring about chronic urological and dyspareunia symptoms
options.C: Expressing visible shock or moral disapproval regarding the practice
options.D: Documenting the precise anatomical classification of the procedure

explanation: Nurses must maintain professional neutrality and empathy; showing disgust or judgment alienates the patient and breaches ethical standards. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary care team essential in the long-term management of FGM complications?

options.A: Because surgical repair can only be performed by a team of at least four physicians
options.B: Because hospital protocols mandate psychiatric evaluation for every female patient
options.C: Because physical, urological, obstetric, and psychological sequelae require diverse clinical expertise
options.D: Because primary nurses are legally prohibited from administering analgesia to survivors

explanation: FGM impacts multiple body systems and mental health, necessitating coordinated care across nursing, surgery, urology, and mental health fields. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h7)

question: What surgical intervention is commonly utilized to relieve chronic urinary retention and enable childbirth in women with Type III FGM?
explanation: De-infibulation surgically opens the fused scar tissue, restoring normal anatomy for the vaginal opening and urinary meatus. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which Nigerian legislative framework explicitly prohibits Female Genital Mutilation and prescribes penalties for offenders?
explanation: The VAPP Act provides a legal foundation across many Nigerian states criminalizing FGM and acts of gender-based violence. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h8)

question: How can community health nurses in Nigeria most effectively contribute to the prevention of FGM?

options.A: By engaging community leaders, traditional birth attendants, and families with educational outreach
options.B: By restricting health education strictly to hospital waiting rooms
options.C: By performing modified versions of the procedure under sterile hospital conditions
options.D: By reporting every pregnant woman to law enforcement agencies automatically

explanation: Sustainable prevention requires community-level dialogue and education that addresses the root cultural drivers of the practice. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h8)
